description: Members without a major are grouped together as their own group. That group counts toward both the total member count and the average group size.

b.request: Group members by `link_to_major` (with NULL majors as one combined group) and list the top 10 groups, highest first, by group count divided by the average group count across all groups, showing each group's major id, member count, share of total members, and that ratio unrounded
b.sql: WITH grouped AS (SELECT link_to_major AS major_id, COUNT(*) AS member_count FROM member GROUP BY link_to_major), totals AS (SELECT SUM(member_count) AS total_members, AVG(member_count) AS avg_group_count FROM grouped) SELECT g.major_id, g.member_count, 1.0 * g.member_count / t.total_members AS share_of_total, 1.0 * g.member_count / t.avg_group_count AS ratio FROM grouped g CROSS JOIN totals t ORDER BY ratio DESC LIMIT 10;

c.request: Group members by their major (`link_to_major`). For each group, show the major id, how many members it has, that count's share of the total, and the count divided by the average group count. List the top 10 by that last ratio, highest first, with no rounding. Members without a major are grouped together as their own group. That group counts toward both the total member count and the average group size.
c.sql: WITH grouped AS (SELECT link_to_major AS major_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM member GROUP BY link_to_major), totals AS (SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_members, COUNT(*) AS group_count, AVG(cnt) AS avg_count FROM grouped) SELECT g.major_id, g.cnt AS member_count, 1.0 * g.cnt / t.total_members AS share, 1.0 * g.cnt / t.avg_count AS ratio FROM grouped g CROSS JOIN totals t ORDER BY ratio DESC LIMIT 10;

a.request: Group the members by their major id (`link_to_major`), treating members with no major as a group of their own. For each group, show the major id, the number of members, that number as a fraction of the total members across all groups, and that number divided by the average member count per group (the average taken over all groups, including the no-major group). Sort by the last ratio from highest to lowest and show only the top 10, without rounding.
a.sql: WITH grouped AS (SELECT NULLIF(TRIM(link_to_major), '') AS major_id, COUNT(*) AS member_count FROM member GROUP BY NULLIF(TRIM(link_to_major), '')), totals AS (SELECT SUM(member_count) AS total_members, COUNT(*) AS group_count FROM grouped) SELECT g.major_id, g.member_count, CAST(g.member_count AS REAL) / t.total_members AS member_fraction, CAST(g.member_count AS REAL) / (CAST(t.total_members AS REAL) / t.group_count) AS ratio_to_avg FROM grouped g CROSS JOIN totals t ORDER BY ratio_to_avg DESC LIMIT 10;

d.request: Members without a major are grouped together as their own group, and that group counts toward both the total member count and the average group size. For each group of members grouped by `link_to_major`, show the major id, the group's member count, that count's share of the total, and the count divided by the average group count, listing the top 10 by that last ratio, highest first, with no rounding.
d.sql:
WITH grp AS (
  SELECT link_to_major AS major_id, COUNT(*) AS member_count
  FROM member
  GROUP BY link_to_major
),
totals AS (
  SELECT SUM(member_count) AS total_members,
         CAST(SUM(member_count) AS REAL) / COUNT(*) AS avg_group_size
  FROM grp
)
SELECT g.major_id,
       g.member_count,
       CAST(g.member_count AS REAL) / t.total_members AS share,
       CAST(g.member_count AS REAL) / t.avg_group_size AS ratio
FROM grp g
CROSS JOIN totals t
ORDER BY ratio DESC
LIMIT 10;
